findings.title: The all_done branch routes to the Account step only when the change has no account, dropping the replace row for an arrival on a completed reopened change
findings.recommendation: Make the all_done clause run the Account step unconditionally (e.g. 'first run the Account step below — it writes a missing account, or replaces the latest when the work since it changed what it says — then congratulate'), so an all_done arrival obeys both complete-apply rows of the lifecycle table. Move the regex in test/core/templates/account-step.test.ts that pins the current wording, and re-record the getApplyChangeSkillTemplate and orbit-apply-change hash pins in test/core/templates/skill-templates-parity.test.ts.
findings.reproduction: orbit-decision-records' delta row 'an apply session that ends with apply complete, on a change that has an account (a walk reopened tasks)' requires a replacement 'at the same point' (before the run summary, or before the completion readout when none is written) whenever the work since the latest account changed what it says — for every such session, an all_done arrival included. Case: a walk reopens a task of change foo (which has account-A); an apply session completes it, changing what foo does, but ends before writing the replacement (the same interruption the 'A resumed session writes a missing account' scenario covers for the no-account case). The next apply session arrives on all_done; apply-change.ts:66 says 'when the change has no account, write it first (the Account step below)' — foo has account-A, so the clause skips the step, and account-A, describing the work before the reopen, stays current. ACCOUNT_STEP's third bullet ('by this session or an earlier one') covers the case, but the all_done clause gates whether the AI reaches it.

findings.title: The glossary's Trail entry lists the trail's contents without the new account/ folder
findings.recommendation: Extend the Trail entry to name the account, e.g. '… and in decisions/ its decision records, and in account/ the change's account', matching docs/cli.md's new orbit emit account paragraph.

commentary: Probed: the account module and its emit-composition wiring read against both delta requirements (scope resolution for explore-only, archived-only, unknown and the literal name archive; the canonical-child identity check, now shared with decisions/ through assertCanonicalChildDir; the shared no-overwrite publish, whose decisions-folder error text is unchanged; the one-chain and replaces checks, including the two-heads case the named limit describes); every trail reader that lists .orbit-runs (chain.ts, orientation.ts, external-runner.ts, archive's recursive copy) to confirm none parses the account/ child; the baseline specs' closed enumerations of the emit command set and of the decisions/ folder, none made false; the generated orbit-apply-change and orbit-address-reviews skills, which carry the steps (address-reviews' Step 7 follows Step 6 and precedes the Commit step). A CLI probe in a disposable project confirmed a refused account exits non-zero with empty stdout and writes no record, though, as for decision records, it leaves the empty .orbit-runs/account/ folder behind, which the spec's after-creation identity check implies. Pass 0 ran inline (tasks, scenario coverage against the ledger and tags, design adherence) and Pass 6 as a scoped residue sweep over the change's renamed and enumerated constructs, both in this worker rather than by invoking verify-change or audit-drift: the brief bars this worker from running another orbit command. The full suite and validate --strict ran green on the live checkout. The pattern: the engine side is tight and well tested; the soft spot is the body prose, where one branch restates the lifecycle table narrower than the table itself.

direction.reasoning: The write gate, its scope and identity checks, and the no-reader guarantee all hold against the specs, and the account the change's own apply session wrote shows the step working. The one divergence is a narrow edge in the apply body's all_done clause — an interrupted session after a reopen — that a one-clause edit and its pins close; it is worth walking before archive because the account feeds the program brief, but it does not call the design into question.
